sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In lesson 11 you said where people were and what they were like: I was at home. Now you'll say what people did: «I cleaned the placemat yesterday», «I chose a bunch of flowers», «we went on a day trip». Actions have a past form for this.

examples.translation: Yesterday I made the placemat clean.

examples.en: I chose a bunch of flowers yesterday.
examples.translation: Yesterday I picked some flowers to buy.

examples.en: We went on a day trip last Sunday.
examples.translation: Last Sunday we went somewhere for one day.
I ate cereal for breakfast.

blocks.text: To say something already happened, you usually add -ed to the action: clean → cleaned, park → parked, visit → visited. You don't need was here: I cleaned, not I was clean.

examples.translation: Yesterday I made the placemat clean.

examples.en: I parked in the parking space yesterday.
examples.translation: Yesterday I left my car in the space.

examples.en: He visited the car wash yesterday.
examples.translation: Yesterday he went to the car wash.
I looked at my licence to be sure.
I said «thank you» to the guide.

fixes.wrong: I was clean the placemat yesterday.

drill.why: Yesterday is the past, so add -ed: visited.

sections.title: The past is the same for everyone

blocks.text: Good news: in the past there's no s for he and she. I cleaned, she cleaned, they cleaned — one form for all.

examples.translation: She opened out the blanket.
He put the tray in another place.
We paid at the parking machine.
She cleaned the front of the car with water.

fixes.wrong: He moves the tea tray yesterday.
fixes.right: He moved the tea tray yesterday.

sections.title: Ends in e — just add d

blocks.text: If the action ends in e, don't add another e: move → moved, use → used, close → closed, untie → untied. In British spelling, travel doubles the l: travelled.

examples.translation: I opened the laces on my shoes.

examples.en: I used the salad bowl yesterday.
examples.translation: I put salad in that bowl.
I shut the back of the car.
We went when the roads were full.

blocks.text: -ed is almost never an extra syllable. After soft «hissing» sounds it sounds like «t»: washed. After voiced sounds, like «d»: cleaned. Only after t or d does it add «id»: wanted, needed, counted.

examples.translation: one syllable, ends in «t»
one syllable, ends in «d»
two syllables: «want-id»
I had to have a roller for fluff.
I found out how many pegs there were.

blocks.text: Don't drop the ending — it's the only thing that shows the past. And don't add «id» after sounds other than t and d.

sections.title: Special words: chose, went, saw, had

blocks.text: Some very common actions change completely in the past, with no -ed. Learn them in pairs: choose → chose, go → went, see → saw, have → had, rise → rose, hide → hid, find → found.

examples.en: I chose a bunch of flowers yesterday.
examples.translation: Yesterday I picked some flowers to buy.
I walked or drove to the shop.

examples.en: The sun rose at six yesterday.
examples.translation: The sun came up at six.
She ate some soft cheese.
I picked a completely new coat.

fixes.wrong: I choosed a bunch of flowers.
fixes.right: I chose a bunch of flowers.

fixes.wrong: He hide the toy car yesterday.
fixes.right: He hid the toy car yesterday.

drill.why: go has a special past form: went.

blocks.text: This form is for things that happened and ended: yesterday, last Sunday, that week. The time words are the same as in lesson 11: yesterday, last Sunday, last night.

examples.en: We went on a day trip last Sunday.
examples.translation: Last Sunday we went somewhere for one day.

examples.en: She went on a school trip yesterday.
examples.translation: Yesterday she went out with her school.
I liked the trip on the boat.

examples.en: We had a fire drill yesterday.
examples.translation: Yesterday we practised leaving for a fire.

fixes.wrong: We go on a day trip last Sunday.
fixes.right: We went on a day trip last Sunday.

blocks.text: If there was an action in the past, use the -ed form or a special word: I checked the airbed. If there was no action and you say what something was like or where, use was or were from lesson 11. Not both.

examples.translation: I looked at the air mattress to be sure.
I put my sleeping bag into the bag.

examples.en: We waited at the meeting point.
examples.translation: We stayed at the place to meet.

fixes.wrong: I was pack my sleeping bag.

drill.hint: One word is extra. Tap it.
drill.fix: With a past action you don't need was: I checked the airbed.

fixes.wrong: He visits the car wash yesterday.
fixes.right: He visited the car wash yesterday.

fixes.wrong: I choosed a bunch of flowers.
fixes.right: I chose a bunch of flowers.

blocks.text: If you see yesterday or last Sunday, look for the past form: -ed or a special word. No s, and no was before the action.
Past actions: -ed — cleaned, used, wanted. One form for everyone. It sounds like «t», «d» or «id». Learn the special words in pairs: chose, went, saw, had, rose, hid, found.

examples.en: I noticed a cycle lane yesterday.
examples.translation: Yesterday I saw a lane for bikes.
She showed her train discount card.
I walked or drove to the shop.
I put the clothes I didn't want into bags.
